records.semanticSummary: The entry describes an occupation involving care of cattle and notes horseback riding as typical; it also separates a film character use.
records.supportedSemanticBoundary: A noun for a worker whose job includes looking after cattle; horseback riding is typical rather than a required condition. The target is the FARM WORKER sense.

records.dictionarySenseSection: Cambridge English Dictionary, UK entry; beat verb — HIT (B2)
records.originalSourceEvidenceLimitation: Frozen Vocab4600 English definition supports DEFEAT only; its Vietnamese gloss additionally lists hit-related translations. Oxford examples support RHYTHM and HEART, but not a separate repeated-hitting definition.
records.ownerAuthorizationReference: Cohort 500-03 CP01 Owner Authorization: Narrow Source-Evidence Remediation (2026-10-11)
records.retrievalMethod: Official Cambridge entry content was returned by web search indexing for the exact Cambridge URL; direct page open returned HTTP 403, so no HTML was retained.
records.semanticSummary: The entry has a verb sense involving successive impacts, with examples of striking a surface or person; the same entry treats defeating a competitor, rhythmic movement, and mixing food as separate senses.
records.supportedSemanticBoundary: A verb sense meaning to hit a person or object repeatedly. Repetition is supported; exceptional force, injury, or violence is not a necessary part of the meaning.
unsupportedClaims: The sense necessarily causes injury or damage.
Making a rhythmic sound or movement.
